heroHeadline: OAS Chief Urges Haiti to Accelerate Voter Registration as PM Vows December Elections 'No Matter What'; Gangs Attack Artibonite Village
heroSubtitle: OAS Secretary General Albert Ramdin concluded a three-day visit to Port-au-Prince on August 19, 2026, warning that voter registration for the December 13 elections 'needs to be accelerated, needs to be intensified' — only around 260,000 voters had registered roughly a month after centers opened, with gang control blocking registration in several municipalities and nearly 1.5 million displaced Haitians facing uncertain voting access. His visit followed PM Alix Didier Fils-Aimé's August 14 declaration that 'the elections will take place this year, no matter what,' as the CEP approved 17 of 18 political groups (228 parties) and prepared a diaspora outreach delegation to the US, Canada, France, Chile, and Brazil. The underlying security crisis persisted: on August 18, Kokorat San Ras and Gran Grif gang members attacked the Marmont Paul locality of Saint-Michel-de-l'Atalaye in Artibonite — a department already accounting for 381 killings, or 25.7% of Haiti's 2026 national total — killing at least one person and burning homes. Earlier in the window, the US Senate's August 11 passage of a two-year HOPE/HELP trade extension and Port-au-Prince's first Criminal Assizes since 2018 (August 13) offered rare institutional bright spots, while Germany's Bundeswehr (August 17) offered airlift support for Gang Suppression Force logistics and opposition figure André Michel publicly demanded restored security ahead of the vote. Inflation continued easing to 18.9% in June 2026, down from 20.0% in May.
